submission.reasoning: On workstation5, svchost.exe (C:\windows\system32\svchost.exe) opened a handle to lsass.exe 6 times over about half a second. The granted access was 0x1000 (PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION), which does not allow reading process memory, so it cannot be used to dump credentials. The call trace runs through the RPC runtime (RPCRT4.dll) into lsm.dll, which is the Local Session Manager service hosted in svchost. That fits normal session-management queries, not a credential-theft tool. The source process is the real system svchost.exe image, and it did nothing else suspicious. Verdict: benign Windows OS activity.
